problems.statement: The spring service change cut recovery/layover time on 21 of 38 routes (median 15% to 8%) with running times unchanged, so buses arrive at terminals with no slack and depart late, propagating lateness; this is the main, systemwide driver of the OTP decline.

Halvorsen Avenue and Bridgeport Road construction (from 2026-04-20) roughly doubled running times through work zones on five routes that also had recovery cut, causing a second, larger OTP step down on Group A and compounding the layover cut; it is a real but localized contributor.
Operator absenteeism (+40%) causing late pull-outs and extraboard scrambles is the cause of the OTP decline, as the Director presents.

The +40% absence figure is largely a measurement artifact: ShiftLine (live 2026-03-30) began auto-recording partial-day absences that the legacy process never counted; full-day absences rose only 1.1%.
Real operational coverage did not worsen: unoperated trips (0.7%), late pull-outs (3.1% vs 3.3%) and extraboard use (41 vs 43/day) are flat in an independent dispatch log.
The OTP measurement itself is unreliable or changed (AVL definition or equipment drift).
Passenger demand, loading, dwell or ramp use increased and slowed service.

Early-leave partial-day absences are elevated on recovery-cut routes (18 vs 10 per 100 operators), plausibly a consequence of no-layover working conditions (no breaks) rather than a cause of lateness; but confounded by seniority, age, route length and garage, and with no pre-April baseline.

Management has not responded to the May schedule grievance and the Director dismisses scheduling and road work, indicating a diagnostic and feedback failure: the problem is attributed to operators rather than to a scheduling decision.

causalClaims.to: Late terminal departures and systemwide OTP decline
Additional OTP drop on Group A routes

causalClaims.from: Timing coincidence of April absence rise and OTP drop

causalClaims.to: Higher early-leave occurrences on those routes

actions.action: Restore recovery time on the 21 routes, prioritizing the five construction-corridor routes (9, 14, 22, 31, 33) and the other long routes, e.g. by adding runtime and buses or trimming Route 51 resources
actions.rationale: The layover cut is the dominant cause and a direct, testable lever; Group B and A both stepped down the week of the change while Group C did not.

actions.action: Re-time the five construction-corridor routes with work-zone running times (about +6.5 min Halvorsen, +5.5 min Bridgeport) for the duration to August 2027, and coordinate detours or transit priority with the City
actions.rationale: Segment data show running time roughly doubled in the zones, which recovery alone cannot absorb.

actions.action: Roll out the tougher attendance policy with discipline at three occurrences in 90 days, counting ShiftLine partial-day occurrences
actions.rationale: The absence rise is a recording artifact, the policy would punish operators for newly counted partial days and for leaving after no-break shifts, and would not fix OTP; it would also inflame the union while the schedule grievance is unanswered.

actions.action: Respond to the May schedule grievance and engage the union on layovers and break time
actions.rationale: It addresses a legitimate operator concern, rebuilds trust and may reduce early leaves.

actions.action: Re-baseline absence reporting (separate full-day and partial-day categories) and correct the board narrative before the November board meeting
actions.rationale: The +40% figure is not comparable across the system change and is driving a mistaken decision.

actions.action: Hire more extraboard operators or add spare capacity as the OTP fix
actions.rationale: Dispatch data show unoperated trips, late pull-outs and extraboard use unchanged, so coverage is not the constraint.

actions.action: Study partial-day early-leave patterns after controlling for seniority, route length and garage, and consider a targeted wellness or relief fix if confirmed
actions.rationale: The link between layover cuts and early leaves is confounded and has no baseline.

actions.action: Track OTP weekly by route group after schedule changes to confirm recovery
actions.rationale: This verifies the causal diagnosis and measures how much of the loss is restored.

nextEvidence: Pilot restoration of recovery time on a subset of Group B routes (or add layover on a few) and compare OTP against matched untreated routes
Partial-day and early-leave occurrences by route, controlling for seniority, route length and garage, plus operator exit-interview or survey input on breaks and layovers
Decomposition of the OTP loss on Group A and B routes into recovery shortfall versus work-zone running time, e.g. trip-level delay propagation analysis
output.summary: The Director's absenteeism theory fails. The +40% rise comes from ShiftLine, live 2026-03-30, which began counting partial-day absences that were never recorded before. Full-day absences rose only 1.1%. The independent dispatch log shows unoperated trips, late pull-outs and extraboard use flat. The real causes are the April 5 layover cuts on 21 routes, which made buses depart late, and construction from April 20 that doubled running times on five of those routes. Untouched routes stayed at 82%. Restore recovery time, retime the construction routes, answer the grievance, and do not roll out the discipline policy, which punishes a measurement artifact.
